newsitem.title: USA: Brent rises in late US trading; arb window closing.
newsitem.headline: Brent rises in late US trading; arb window closing.

text.p: North Sea Brent rose in late U.S. trading Wednesday with a major Wall Street player again attributed with most of the buying, traders said.
A full boat of paper March Brent changed hands at $22.50 a barrel, up four cents from the IPE settlement.
Three partial March Brents traded a total of 500 times, all at $22.50 a barrel.
February/March and March/April Brent each moved at 45 cents, traders said.
Meanwhile, the transatlantic arbitrage window is beginning to close, traders said.
The spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent was around $1.50-55 a barrel Wednesday, down some 10-20 cents from last week.
Only two companies, both based in the United States, are offering Brent cargoes into the Gulf Coast for March delivery.
The price for March 10-15 delivery is around March WTI minus 12 cents a barrel, while March 20-24 delivery is going for around March WTI minus 35-36 cents, traders said.
"It's real skinny," said one Gulf Coast refiner commenting on the scarcity of offers. "I would say the window is shut."
Even Latin American pickings are slim. Colombian state-owned Ecopetrol is offering a Cusiana cargo for loading March 6. The crude last traded at April WTI minus 28 cents, traders said.
Elsewhere, three Argentine oil producers signed a new term contract for Escalante crude with a U.S. Gulf Coast refiner, trade sources said.
The six-month deal supplies the refiner with 12,000 barrels per day (bpd) of low-sulfur, 23-API gravity Escalante beginning in April.
The price was set at benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus $3.14 a barrel fob Caleta Cordoba, the sources said.
The new contract supplants a one-year term deal with Brazil's state-owned Petrobras which expires in March. The Brazilian contract was priced at a discount of $3.21 a barrel, the sources said.
The Argentine producers are Astra, Compania Naviera Perez Companc and Tecpetrol.

In Ecuador, operations on the main TransEcaudoran pipeline are running normally despite a 48-hour general strike. Oil exports have also remained uninterrupted, an official from state-owned Petroecuador told Reuters by telephone.
